sections.label: Women's Charter marriage principles
sections.summary: The Women's Charter upholds principles that marriage is the cornerstone of family formation and that marriages here must be genuine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The Women's Charter upholds our overarching principles towards marriage and divorce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: These are, for marriage, that marriage is the cornerstone of family formation and, thus, the significance of the solemnisation and registration of marriages must be emphasised; the institution of marriage must be protected by ensuring that all marriages contracted here are genuine.

sections.label: Our Marriage Journey portal
sections.summary: MSF will introduce the Our Marriage Journey portal this year for couples to complete all pre-solemnisation steps online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) will, therefore, introduce the new "Our Marriage Journey" portal this year, which will enable couples to conveniently complete all pre-solemnisation steps online.

sections.label: Video-link marriage solemnisation
sections.summary: Clause 15 introduces section 24 to let the Registrar and licensed solemnisers solemnise marriages via video-link in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Clause 15 also introduces a new section 24 to empower the Registrar and licensed solemnisers to solemnise marriages via video-link in Singapore should couples choose to do so.

sections.label: Cancelling Notice of Marriage
sections.summary: Clause 10 introduces section 15 to allow the Notice of Marriage to be cancelled where the Registrar is satisfied there is good reason.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Lastly, clause 10 introduces a new section 15 to allow the Notice of Marriage to be cancelled where the Registrar is satisfied that there is good reason to do so.

sections.label: Portal features and JOY mentoring
sections.summary: The portal will provide marriage preparation information, a Marriage Questionnaire, programme sign-ups and tips, while the JOY pilot lets solemnisers mentor newlyweds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The "Our Marriage Journey" portal will also: (a) provide information and resources on marriage preparation; (b) provide an online Marriage Questionnaire tool to help couples prepare for their next step; (c) recommend and facilitate sign-ups for suitable Marriage Preparation Programmes; and (d) provide push notifications of online marriage tips to couples in their first year of marriage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Many licensed solemnisers develop good relationships with the couples and have a wealth of helpful tips.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We are therefore piloting the "Journey with You" initiative, referred to as JOY, in short, which will enable licensed solemnisers to mentor newlyweds in the first year of marriage.

sections.label: Stricter requirements for marrying here
sections.summary: Clause 10 introduces section 18, letting the Minister prescribe a stay length, intended as 31 continuous days, for non-citizen or non-PR parties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Going forward, we will impose stricter requirements for such persons to marry here.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Clause 10 of the amendment Bill introduces section 18, of which subsection (1)(c) provides that where any party is not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, the Minister may prescribe the length of stay required by at least one party in Singapore before they can be allowed to marry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We intend to prescribe that at least one party must have been physically present in Singapore for 31 continuous days.

sections.label: New sixth fact for divorce
sections.summary: Clause 29 repeals section 95 and enacts section 95A, adding divorce by mutual agreement of irretrievable breakdown as a sixth fact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Many divorcees we spoke to shared that until the divorce is final, they could not focus on their children, though they wanted to.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Hence, in line with the Family Justice Courts' approach of therapeutic justice, clause 29 repeals the current section 95 and enacts a new section 95A, to introduce divorce by mutual agreement of the irretrievable breakdown of marriage as a sixth fact that parties may cite to show that their marriage has irretrievably broken down.

sections.label: Requirements for mutual agreement divorce
sections.summary: Parties relying on the sixth fact must submit reasons, reconciliation efforts, and considerations on children and financial affairs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Under the new section 95A(1)(f) and subsection (6)(a), parties may rely on this sixth fact if they mutually agree that the marriage has broken down irretrievably, but this is not a simple "handshake" of a mutual agreement to divorce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Instead, parties will submit to the Court: the reasons leading them to conclude that their marriage has irretrievably broken down; the efforts made to reconcile; and considerations given to the arrangements to be made in relation to their children and financial affairs.

sections.label: Court must reject if reconciliation possible
sections.summary: Subsection (6)(c) states the Court must reject any agreement if reconciliation is reasonably possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Lastly, subsection (6)(c) states that the Court must reject any agreement if the Court considers that reconciliation is reasonably possible.

sections.label: Existing divorce safeguards continue
sections.summary: All safeguards of the current divorce framework continue, including the three-year time bar and three-month period before finalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: All safeguards of the divorce framework today will continue to apply, including the three-year time bar on filing for divorce and the three-month period before the divorce is finalised.

sections.label: Parties explain mutual agreement basis
sections.summary: Parties must explain the basis for their mutual agreement, reconciliation attempts, and considerations on financial affairs and children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Parties must explain the basis for their mutual agreement on the irretrievable breakdown of their marriage, what attempts they have made at reconciliation and what considerations they have in regard to their financial affairs and children.

sections.label: Court power to reject agreement
sections.summary: The Court may reject an agreement to divorce if a reasonable possibility of reconciliation remains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The Court has the power to reject an agreement to divorce if there remains a reasonable possibility of reconciliation.

sections.label: Divorce balance in DMA framework
sections.summary: The DMA framework balances marriage as a public institution with permitting divorce when a marriage has truly broken down, without unnecessary acrimony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: One party also cannot, unilaterally, divorce the other.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Therefore, the DMA framework strikes a balance between two principles: one, that marriage is a public institution and divorce is a serious matter; and, two, when a marriage has truly broken down, the law should permit a divorce without creating unnecessary acrimony.

sections.label: Extending MPP to simplified divorce
sections.summary: MSF will amend the Women's Charter (Parenting Programme) Rules to extend MPP to all parents with minor children on the simplified divorce track.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: However, MSF's 2020 Study on Co-Parenting Styles showed that regardless whether respondents reported an uncontested or contested divorce, the proportion of divorcees who reported practising cooperative co-parenting among uncontested and contested divorces are similar.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Hence, we will amend the Women's Charter (Parenting Programme) Rules to extend MPP to all parents with minor children on the simplified divorce track.

sections.label: Court advising children's programme attendance
sections.summary: Clause 36 introduces section 132A allowing the Court to advise parents to secure a child's attendance at the Programme for Children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: For children, the programme educates them on positive ways to cope with their parents' divorce and skills to share their feelings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: However, out of about 6,500 children affected by divorce annually between 2016 and 2020, fewer than 200 attend the Children-in-Between programme annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The divorce process should prioritise the best interest of the child and ensure that children are supported.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 36 introduces a new section 132A to allow the Court to advise parents to secure the child's attendance at the Programme for Children at any stage of the proceedings or after the final judgment has been granted if the Court thinks that this would be beneficial.

sections.label: Court orders for access breaches
sections.summary: The Court may order additional access, compensation, counselling or programmes, a bond, and as a last resort imprisonment or a fine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The Court may order: (a) the care and control parent to grant the access parent additional access to the child to make up for the access denied; (b) the care and control parent to compensate the access parent for expenses incurred as a result of the breach of order; (c) both parties and the child, or any of them, to attend counselling, mediation, therapeutic or educational programmes or family support programmes; (d) the care and control parent to enter into a bond to ensure future compliance with the order; and (e) as a last resort, imprisonment or a fine for the care and control parent.

sections.label: Maintenance enforcement process feedback
sections.summary: Feedback raised that maintenance enforcement processes are time- and resource-intensive, adversarial for litigants-in-person, and should distinguish those who cannot pay from those who will not.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: During our engagements with stakeholders, issues were raised regarding the current maintenance enforcement processes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We received feedback that (a) these processes are time- and resource-intensive for wives, ex-wives and mothers who tend to be on the receiving end of the payment of maintenance; (b) the current adversarial Court processes are challenging for applicants who are mostly litigants-in-person; and (c) there is a need to distinguish between respondents who cannot pay and those who will not pay, to provide different interventions to address the underlying issues for the two groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We recognise that maintenance enforcement processes can be further enhanced and MSF is working with MinLaw and the Family Justice Courts to study how to provide more efficient and effective enforcement of maintenance orders and minimise repeat enforcement.

sections.label: Married woman's equal rights
sections.summary: New section 50(1) provides that a married woman's rights, privileges, powers, capacities, duties and liabilities are the same as a married man's, unless otherwise provided in written law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: There is no doubt that a married woman is and should be the equal of a married man, not just in specific areas or for specific purposes, but as a general principle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This principle is enshrined in the new section 50(1), which provides that the rights, privileges, powers, capacities, duties and liabilities of a married woman are the same as those of a married man, unless otherwise provided for in any written law.

sections.label: Family violence protection Bill
sections.summary: A separate Bill will enhance protection against family violence by the end of this year, following Taskforce recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In particular, in line with the Taskforce on Family Violence's recommendations, we will enhance the protection against family violence in a separate Bill by the end of this year.

sections.label: Marriage and divorce amendments
sections.summary: The amendments mainly let both men and women make decisions about marriage, divorce and family, and make these decisions binding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The amendments are, in the main, to allow both men and women to make decisions about marriage, divorce and family and then, for laws to make these decisions binding.

sections.label: Child-centric custody and mothers' employment
sections.summary: Having decided to part ways, custody is child-centric, but provisions for parents, especially mothers, in employment matters may need closer look.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Having decided to part ways, we have decided, in terms of custody, to be “child-centric”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I wonder, however, if we ought to take a closer look at provisions for parents, especially mothers, in employment matters.

sections.label: Employment support for divorced women
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Court-ordered mediation and counselling can include employment advice for unemployed women at divorce, and calls for flexible work support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For example, can we ask for Court-ordered interventions, such as mediation and counselling, to include employment advice and assistance for women who are unemployed at the point of divorce?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I also call for better flexible work support for employees at all life stages, especially mothers with caregiving duties, and career development for back-to-work women.

sections.label: New divorce fact in Clause 29
sections.summary: Clause 29 introduces a new fact for divorce: spouses agreeing in writing that the marriage has irretrievably broken down, stating reasons, reconciliation efforts and financial and child arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 29 of the Bill introduces a new fact that can be relied upon to file for a divorce: that the marriage has broken down due to the spouses' agreeing that there has been an irretrievable breakdown.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to rely on this new fact, the spouses must enter into an agreement in writing, stating their reasons for concluding that the marriage has broken down, what efforts they have made to reconcile and what considerations they have given to the arrangements concerning their financial affairs and any child of the marriage.

sections.label: Shorter separation for agreed divorce
sections.summary: Spouses living apart can agree to divorce after much shorter separation than three years, such as six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, if the spouses have been living apart, they can agree to divorce if they have been separated for much shorter periods than three years; say, for just six months.

sections.label: Court rewriting DMA agreements
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether the Court may still endorse a one-sided DMA agreement but rewrite financial and children arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this regard, I do acknowledge the point made by the Minister of State earlier that this can also happen in other types of divorce, not just DMA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But specifically, regarding DMA, I have this clarification: if the Court comes across an agreement that is clearly one-sided or detrimental to the children, am I right to assume that the Court may still endorse DMA, but rewrite the arrangements regarding finances and children?

sections.label: Enforcement of maintenance orders
sections.summary: Defaulting parents force innocent parents to take out further enforcement proceedings, and the Government plans enhancements under the Family Justice Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If the defaulting parent defaults again, the onus is on the innocent parent once again to take out further enforcement proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Although not covered in this Bill, I note that there are plans by the Government to provide a more efficient and effective means to enforce maintenance orders and to minimise the need for repeat enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was stated in the Ministry's press release of 1 November on this Bill that the Government is looking into making enhancements to the enforcement of maintenance orders under another law, the Family Justice Act, which will be tabled some time this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And earlier, the Minister of State confirmed this as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is absolutely necessary to reduce the burden on the parent who is simply seeking to obtain for themselves and their children what is due from an ex-spouse.

sections.label: Stay-at-home fathers in Singapore
sections.summary: MOM's Labour Force in Singapore Report recorded about 1,500 stay-at-home fathers in 2017, up 700 from a decade earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: According to MOM's Labour Force in Singapore Report, there were about 1,500 stay-at-home fathers in 2017, an increase of 700 from a decade earlier.

sections.label: Men seeking maintenance
sections.summary: The Women's Charter was amended in 2016 to allow ill, disabled or ex-husbands to seek maintenance from ex-wives if incapacitated and unable to support themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: While men were previously not allowed to seek maintenance, amendments were earlier made to the Women's Charter in 2016 to allow ill, disabled or ex-husbands to seek maintenance from their ex-wives if they are incapacitated, unable to support themselves.

sections.label: Man ordered to pay maintenance
sections.summary: In 2014 The Straits Times reported a retired man ordered to pay $70,000 maintenance to his former wife, who earned more than him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2014, The Straits Times reported an instance of a man who was ordered to pay $70,000 in maintenance to his former wife despite the fact that he was retired, she earned more than him and he paid the mortgage of their marital home.

sections.label: Divorce cases using simplified procedures
sections.summary: Currently, about 60% of divorce cases have been filed through the simplified procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Currently, about 60% of the divorce cases have been filed through the simplified procedures.

sections.label: Support for less adversarial divorce
sections.summary: The Member supports a less adversarial divorce path without needing to blame either party, to reduce conflict, especially for those with fewer resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Like many Members of this House, I was brought up to believe that marriage is a beautiful thing – something to be protected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But like the Members who have spoken before me and most family law practitioners and women's groups, I support the proposal that providing a less adversarial, more amicable path for divorce and settlement of disputes, without the need to blame either party for adultery, desertion or unreasonable behaviour, will help to reduce conflict during a most difficult time, especially for those with less resources to lawyer up.

sections.label: US and UK reconciliation studies
sections.summary: Studies in the US and UK show about 10% of divorces involve openness to reconcile or are averted with counselling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the US, studies have shown that in about 10% of divorces, both parties are often open to efforts to reconcile and, recently, in the UK, the same percentage, 10% of divorce proceedings started, are averted with counselling.

sections.label: Resident's eight-year access fight
sections.summary: A resident did not see his son for eight years while fighting in Court for access rights at great financial and career cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One of my residents did not see his son for eight years, during which he fought in Court for his access rights at great cost to his finances and his career.

sections.label: Parental alienation and family law accreditation
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Government will review the definition of parental alienation and consider mandatory accreditation, standards and monitoring for family law professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Six, will the Government undertake a review of the definition of parental alienation, which is currently not tracked, to ensure it can be tracked and to facilitate reforms to protect the rights, interests and physical, mental and financial health of alienated parents and, by extension, their children?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Seven, finally, given that no area of law matters to more people than family law, will the Government consider the establishment of mandatory accreditation, standards and monitoring processes, including complaints mechanisms and ongoing professional development and training requirements for family consultants, counsellors and all family law professionals, including judges, also in the areas of family violence and child abuse, unconscious bias, parental alienation dynamics, engaging and communicating with children and disability awareness?

sections.label: Clause 35 custody enforcement powers
sections.summary: Clause 35 introduces new sections 126A and 126B to the Women's Charter to enhance the Court's enforcement powers for custody and child access orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Clause 35 of the Bill introduces new sections 126A and 126B to the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: These two sections seek to enhance the enforcement powers of the Court relating to custody and child access orders.

sections.label: Fine or imprisonment for defaulting parent
sections.summary: New section 126B(3)(e) gives the Court power to sentence a defaulting parent to a fine or imprisonment term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: First, the new section 126B(3)(e) provides power to the Court to sentence a defaulting parent to a fine or imprisonment term.

sections.label: Counselling workload and divorces
sections.summary: Counselling can be long-drawn, and with about 7,000 divorces yearly, counsellors will be stretched without enough trained counsellors to share the workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Counselling can be a long-drawn process and, with about 7,000 divorces every year, these counsellors will be stretched if there are not enough trained counsellors to share the workload.

sections.label: Concern over mutual agreement divorce
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether new section 95A(1)(f) will make it easier for couples who cannot resolve disputes to apply for divorce by mutual agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: My concern is whether the new section 95A(1)(f) will make it easier for couples who cannot work out their disputes to take the easy way out and apply for divorce based on mutual agreement.

sections.label: Simplified Track divorce share
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported on 8 November last year that Simplified Track divorce accounts for 60% of divorce applications filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Straits Times reported on 8 November last year that Simplified Track divorce accounts for 60% of the divorce applications filed.

sections.label: Divorce and marriage numbers
sections.summary: Last year there were 6,959 divorces and 22,651 registered marriages, and the speaker asks why a new clause for divorce by mutual agreement is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Last year, there were 6,959 divorces and 22,651 registered marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Given the above facts and circumstances, may I ask Minister of State why is there a need to introduce this new clause to allow divorce by mutual agreement, or DMA?

sections.label: California no-fault divorce study
sections.summary: NCCS cited a study that after the first no-fault divorce was adopted in California, marriage rates persistently declined with more single parenthood and cohabitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: NCCS cited a study that said that after the first “no-fault divorce” was adopted in California, there was a persistent decline in marriage rates, accompanied by more single parenthood and cohabitation.

sections.label: MSF feedback and section 95A(6)
sections.summary: MSF cited strong feedback against citing fault and dredging up the past, but section 95A(6) still requires parties to state in writing reasons and reconciliation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In the media release by MSF, the Government cited that there was strong feedback against having to cite fault against the other party and having to dredge up the past just to prove the facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, section 95A(6) still requires parties to state in writing the reasons leading X and Y to conclude that their marriage has irretrievably broken down and their efforts made to reconcile.

sections.label: Divorce balance assurance sought
sections.summary: The Government must balance making divorce too difficult against making it too easy, and the speaker seeks assurance it is not taking the latter approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Government has to strike a balance between making it too difficult for parties in failed marriages to get a divorce versus making it too easy for couples to give up their commitment and call it quits when they encounter difficulties in their marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I seek the Government's assurance that we are not taking the latter approach.

sections.label: Irretrievably broken down marriages section
sections.summary: The new section for marriages irretrievably broken down is a good step to make divorce less acrimonious, especially with children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The new section inserted for marriages that have "irretrievably broken down" is a good step forward to make the divorce process less acrimonious for parties involved, particularly if there are children already in the marriage.

sections.label: Avoiding dragged-out divorce process
sections.summary: The section strives to avoid dragging out divorce for couples trapped in unhappy marriages seeking peaceful resolution while awaiting legal processes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What this section strives to achieve though is to avoid dragging out the divorce process for couples who are already trapped in an unhappy marriage and are aiming for a peaceful resolution but are just waiting for the legal processes to go through.

sections.label: Support for children of divorce
sections.summary: This will help children of divorce adapt and cope, and MSF is introducing programmes for them and expanding family support programme attendance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will help children of divorce to better adapt and cope with the divorce process.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, also happy that MSF has also decided to introduce programmes for the children of divorces and to expand the groups of people who have to attend family support programmes.

sections.label: Community and religious organisations' role
sections.summary: Community and religious organisations can assist mediation and counselling, and the speaker hopes these resources extend to Muslim marriages under AMLA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Community and religious organisations also have a part to play to assist in the mediation and counselling processes as faith-based teachings can also be tapped on to achieve the best outcomes for suitable couples.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I actually hope that these resources will also be tapped on to offer marital and divorce counselling support and that the positive changes here will also be extended to Muslim marriages, though they are not administered by the Women's Charter but by AMLA.

sections.label: Parliament support after divorce
sections.summary: Parliament must invest time to understand divorce struggles and provide support, so the Labour Movement welcomes the Women's Charter amendments for divorce programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet, as we recognise that the dissolution of marriage has become more common in today's day and age, this Parliament, as leaders of society, must look to invest time and effort to understand not only the struggles of divorce, but also to provide the requisite support individuals need in the aftermath of such a decision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that the Labour Movement welcomes the amendments to the Women's Charter as we look not only to enhancing marriage processes but, more importantly, providing greater support for couples through divorce programmes for parents and kin in the midst of the proceedings.

sections.label: NTUC aid for single mothers
sections.summary: Since 2009, NTUC has helped single mothers find work through women-focused job fairs with e2i and LearningHUB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Since 2009, when Mdm Halimah Yacob launched the "We Care for U" project to help single mothers find work, the NTUC has made a concerted effort to render aid to single mothers to find work through women-focused job fairs done with the e2i as well as our LearningHUB.

sections.label: Support for newly-single mothers
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Court programmes for children and family support, and calls for counselling, flexible work and childcare for newly-single mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The current amendments to expand the legal remit of our Courts to prescribe programmes for children and family support during divorce proceedings are most welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But I hope that such efforts would also be extended to newly-single mothers who could very well benefit from Court-ordered interventions to be provided with counselling for employment, financial and housing assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Furthermore, this responsibility to provide support does not rest solely on the shoulders of our Courts, as employers play an important role in facilitating an environment that welcomes our newly-single mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to seek better flexible work support for employees at all life stages but, particularly mothers with dependants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: An enhancement of our existing Tripartite Standard for Flexible Work Arrangements could be a great step in looking to provide special assistance for single mothers who bear the sole responsibility of providing for their children and dependants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: If the school is near their workplaces or homes, it would be a much-welcomed relief as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It, hence, becomes clear that specialised assistance goes beyond employment alone as the greater availability and accessibility of dependable and perhaps even prioritised support networks, such as childcare centres and after-school programmes for single mothers, become more important.

sections.label: Divorce laws for divorced women
sections.summary: The speaker calls for more social protection and support for divorced women through this amendment to the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Once again, we would like to call for more understanding and ways to provide social protection and support to divorced women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that we must provide better and more reasonable divorce laws for divorce cases through this amendment to the Women's Charter.

sections.label: Marriage and divorce statistics
sections.summary: The speaker says the amendments are a step in the right direction, citing falling average marriages and divorces and 2020's lowest divorce figure since 2006.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Although more can be done, the current amendments to the Women's Charter are a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to the latest Statistics on Marriages and Divorces in Singapore, the annual average number of marriages fell in the last five years from 27,635 to 26,255, compared to the period between 2011 and 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Similarly, there is a slight decrease in the annual average number of divorces from 7,439 to 7,424, compared to the previous five-year period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is, however, heartening to know that the figure for divorce for 2020 was 6,959, the lowest since 2006.

sections.label: Nevada divorce rate
sections.summary: Nevada has one of the highest divorce rates in the United States, nearly 21 divorces per 1,000 married women in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Similarly, this has also impacted the divorce rate in Nevada, which has one of the highest divorce rates in the United States, with a rate of nearly 21 divorces per 1,000 married women in 2019.

sections.label: Syariah Court marriage counselling
sections.summary: In Syariah Court divorce proceedings, parties must attend the Marriage Counselling Programme before filing for divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In divorce proceedings before the Syariah Court, parties are required to attend the Marriage Counselling Programme before they can file an application for divorce.

sections.label: Parenting programmes for divorcing parents
sections.summary: Parties with a child below 21 must complete a Parenting Programme and, before collecting the Divorce Certificate, undergo Parenting PACT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In addition, if parties have a child below 21 years old, they must also complete a Parenting Programme during the Marriage Counselling Programme to discuss post-divorce co-parenting plans at the Marriage Counselling Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: After the divorce, before parties are allowed to collect the Divorce Certificate, if they have at least one child below 21 years old, they must undergo a family support programme known as “Parenting PACT” to help them better understand the impact of parental divorce on children.

sections.label: Mandatory counselling for children
sections.summary: About 200 children undergo such programmes, under 5% of 6,000 affected children, and the speaker suggests making counselling mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: I heard from the Minister of State just now at the Second Reading opening speech that around 200 children undergo such programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: That is less than 5% of the 6,000 or so affected children whose parents are undergoing divorce proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: First, perhaps counselling and attendance of programme for children should be made mandatory either before the commencement of FJC proceedings or before the final judgment or divorce certificate can be issued or collected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Second, for couples with at least one child aged between six and 14, perhaps counselling and such programmes should be made mandatory for the same reasons as earlier stated.

sections.label: Assessment and penalties for breach
sections.summary: The passage asks whether an objective assessment such as a social welfare report would be commissioned, and notes fines up to $20,000 or 12 months' jail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Would there be an objective assessment before determination, for example, that a social welfare report be commissioned?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: And in respect of the punitive punishment aspect, as stated, the parent in breach can be fined up to $20,000 or jailed up to 12 months or both.

sections.label: Variation of care and control orders
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Courts should be empowered to order a reversal of care and control instead of a jail term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Would it be better to empower the Courts to order a variation of the care and control order, that is, a reversal of the care and control, instead of a jail term?

sections.label: Shared care and control orders rising
sections.summary: Courts increasingly order shared care and control, comprising 9.5% of judgments in 2020, up from 5.6% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We know that our Courts are increasingly ordering divorced parents to have shared care and control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Such orders have almost doubled in recent times, comprising 9.5% of Court judgments in 2020, up from 5.6% in 2016.

sections.label: HDB appeals and rental flats
sections.summary: Since 2016, HDB granted 13 of 20 such appeals and approved seven rental flat applications related to shared care and control cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Since 2016, HDB has granted 13 out of 20 such appeals and approved another seven rental flat applications related to shared care and control cases.

sections.label: Children-in-Between Programme counselling
sections.summary: Speaker calls the programme good and asks the Ministry to make it mandatory for children whose parents are divorcing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is an exceptionally good programme that provides counselling and support for children whose parents are undergoing divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I raised this previously and am again calling for the Ministry to consider making it mandatory for all children whose parents are undergoing a divorce.

sections.label: Low programme attendance
sections.summary: Less than 2% of children affected by divorce attend the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, and unfortunately, less than 2% of children affected by divorce attend this programme.

sections.label: Online misogyny and Women's Charter
sections.summary: AWARE and Quilt.AI research found online misogyny claims men are unprotected by law, and speaker suggests moving Charter provisions to criminal statutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Research by AWARE and Quilt.AI found that one of the main narratives in online misogyny is that "men are unprotected by the law." The problem is summed up by one of the examples cited in the research: "Where is the Men's Charter?" Undoubtedly, we know these voices are wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am aware that Part 11 and other provisions of the Charter are specific to crimes related to women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can move them to the relevant criminal statutes, such as the Penal Code.

sections.label: Renaming Women's Charter proposals
sections.summary: Speaker says renaming alone is not enough and lists three points, including renaming the Women's Charter to the Family Charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The renaming would help reshape minds, but it would not be enough by itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We will continue to need changes in laws and mindsets to make progress on the road towards gender equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In summary, my points today are: one, that the Ministry should make flat applications easier for parents with shared care and control; two, the Ministry should mandate the Children-in-Between Programme for children with divorced parents; and three, that we rename the Women's Charter to the Family Charter.

sections.label: Three-year marriage before divorce
sections.summary: Couples in Singapore must commit to marriage for at least three years before divorce, barring exceptional circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Couples in Singapore must commit to marriage for at least three years before any sort of divorce is allowed, barring exceptional circumstances.

sections.label: Strengthening Families Programme launch
sections.summary: A new Strengthening Families Programme was launched where 10 Family Service Centres offer services on marriage, finances and parenting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last November, a new Strengthening Families Programme was launched, where 10 Family Service Centres will offer specialised services to address issues related to marriage, finances and parenting.

sections.label: Mandatory counselling for pre-divorce couples
sections.summary: The speaker asks about remedial action if couples miss counselling and proposes extending mandatory counselling to pre-divorce couples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Is there remedial action if the couple does not attend subsequent counselling sessions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I wish to propose that the Government consider extending mandatory counselling to pre-divorce couples.

sections.label: Mandatory pre-divorce counselling proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes mandatory pre-divorce counselling for every couple, with or without children, before filing for a no-fault divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The mandatory parenting programme, presently, only applies when there is a child from the marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will be beneficial for every couple, with or without children, to go for mandatory pre-divorce counselling before they can file for a no-fault divorce.

sections.label: Couples awaiting no-fault divorce law
sections.summary: The speaker says couples await the no-fault divorce law to divorce civilly without waiting three years and agree pre-divorce counselling would help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, they are looking forward to the passing of the new no-fault divorce law so that they can divorce civilly and move on, without waiting for another three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They have no wish to take the matter to Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They agreed that some form of pre-divorce counselling to help them navigate the financial and emotional implications of their decisions would be helpful.

sections.label: Normalising marital counselling
sections.summary: The speaker says the next step is to normalise marital counselling, encourage early professional help, and set aside necessary resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The next step is to normalise marital counselling and encourage couples to seek professional help at the early onset of problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is all a part of improving communication and strengthening relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must set aside the necessary resources to achieve this.

sections.label: Digitally-registered marriages in Singpass
sections.summary: The speaker asks how digitally-registered marriages will be reflected in Singpass.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, how will digitally-registered marriages be reflected in our Singpass?

sections.label: Making courses mandatory
sections.summary: The speaker says courses are optional but suggests they be made mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Courses are optional but I would suggest that they be made mandatory.

sections.label: Solemniser training and divorce by mutual agreement
sections.summary: Recommends solemnisers be trained on assistance programmes and supports a sixth fact of divorce by mutual agreement, with reconciliation efforts submitted to the Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, recommend that solemnisers undergo training and be updated on the assistance programmes available so that they can be a source of emotional support and point couples who seek their help to the appropriate agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I support the introduction of a sixth fact of "divorce by mutual agreement of the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage", or DMA, for short.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under this fact, efforts to reconcile will have to be submitted to the Court.

sections.label: Renaming Women's Charter to Family Charter
sections.summary: Supports amendments to make divorce less acrimonious and requests renaming the Women's Charter to Family Charter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support the current amendments to make divorce less acrimonious to protect the well-being of all parties involved and to enable better post-divorce emotional healing for all parties, especially for children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, my first request is the change in the name of the "Women’s Charter" to "Family Charter".

sections.label: Husbands applying for maintenance from wives
sections.summary: Says husbands should be entitled to apply for maintenance from wives where necessary, going beyond the 2016 amendment for sick or incapacitated husbands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Husbands should be entitled to apply for maintenance from their wives where the circumstances are necessary and appropriate, both during and after marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2016, the Women’s Charter was amended to allow husbands to apply for maintenance from their wives if they are sick or incapacitated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can go beyond that, to allow for husbands to apply for maintenance from wives, if the distribution of labour between the spouses during marriage favoured the earning potential of the wife to be realised instead of the husband’s.

sections.label: Rewording offences against women and girls
sections.summary: Says clauses around offences against women and girls should be reworded to be gender neutral.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, for the clauses around “offences against women and girls”, we will do well to reword them to be gender neutral.

sections.label: Average marriage ages in Singapore
sections.summary: States the average Singaporean man gets married three years later and the average Singaporean woman five years later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The average Singaporean man gets married three years later and the average Singaporean woman five years later.

sections.label: Exceptional hardship clause for early divorce
sections.summary: States there is a clause allowing exceptional hardship for divorce before three years, which is open to subjective interpretation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While there currently is a clause that allows for "exceptional hardship" for divorce before three years is up, it is open to subjective interpretation.

sections.label: Divorce time bar and fault evidence
sections.summary: The speaker recommends reducing the divorce time bar to one year for all couples and supports the Bill, welcoming an amendment that removes the need to provide evidence of each other's faults.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If the data shows that most of them end in divorce anyway, I recommend the time bar for divorce be reduced to one year for all couples.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these, which I hope can be considered in future amendments, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.39 pm until 4.00 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I welcome this amendment which I feel will help reduce the agony and bitterness during the difficult process of divorce, since neither party will have to provide evidence of each other's faults.

sections.label: Registrar discretion on marriages of convenience
sections.summary: The Registrar has discretion to require couples to perform pre-solemnisation steps in person where there are concerns such as suspected marriages of convenience, which some foreigners abuse to stay or work illegally in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This situation is to be avoided at all costs and the risk of confrontational exchanges must be minimised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There is a provision for the Registrar to have the discretion to require any couple to perform any pre-solemnisation step in person where there may be concerns, such as suspected marriages of convenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, there has been quite a number of foreigners who abuse the system and marry for convenience to stay or work, sometimes illegally, in Singapore.

sections.label: Illegal partnerships and criminal links
sections.summary: Such illegal partnerships undermine the institution of marriage and are often linked to criminal and vice activities that damage society's fabric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Not only are such illegal partnerships undermining our institution of marriage, but they are also often linked to criminal and vice activities which damage the fabric of our society.

sections.label: Court-ordered counselling for child access
sections.summary: New section 126B empowers the Court to order parties to attend therapeutic programmes or counselling to better manage parental hostilities and spare the child from choosing sides.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The new section 126B, in relation to the enforcement of child access orders, empowers the Court to order, inter alia, the parties to attend therapeutic programmes or counselling in the hope that the hostilities between parents can be better managed and that the child is spared from choosing sides.

sections.label: Supervised visitation costs and regional centres
sections.summary: Supervised visitations by a counsellor on Saturdays at the DSSA cost $240 per hour, and by the end of FY2022 there will be 10 regional centres to support families in need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Visitations which will be supervised by a counsellor on a Saturday at the DSSA will cost $240 per hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: By the end of FY2022, there will be 10 regional centres available to support families in need.

sections.label: Divorce by mutual agreement
sections.summary: The new amendment introduces a sixth fact, divorce by mutual agreement of the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage, as a possible solution for parties mutually agreeing to dissolve the marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The new amendment, which introduces the sixth fact, termed divorce by mutual agreement of the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage, may be a new solution to those parties who are in mutual agreement to dissolve the marriage.

sections.label: Sixth fact reconciliation efforts
sections.summary: Under the new sixth fact, parties must also show efforts at marital reconciliation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Under the new sixth fact, the parties will also have to show efforts at marital reconciliation.

sections.label: Children of divorced families outcomes
sections.summary: Children from divorced families are less likely to complete university, may earn lower salaries, and are more inclined to remain single and predisposed to divorce by 35.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Compared to children whose parents were not separated, children from divorced families are less likely to complete University, may earn comparatively lower salaries and are more inclined to remain single and are predisposed to divorce if they are married by the age of 35.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, can the Ministry clarify if this means that this fact can be relied upon only when the divorce is filed under the Simplified Track where parties have agreed on all issues relating to the divorce and the ancillary matters?

sections.label: Uncontested divorce amended claim
sections.summary: The question asks whether Courts could allow divorce to proceed uncontested on an amended claim under the sixth fact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this case, could the Courts allow the divorce to be proceeded with on an uncontested basis on an amended claim under the sixth fact?

sections.label: Rationale for new divorce concept
sections.summary: MSF said divorcees' feedback was that citing a fault-based fact dredges up unhappy memories and can make proceedings acrimonious, harming children's emotional well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The rationale for introducing such a concept, as explained by MSF, arose from feedback from divorcees that having to cite one of the current fault-based facts as the reason for divorce dredges up unhappy memories and can cause the divorce proceedings to turn acrimonious, thus making it detrimental to the emotional well-being of their children.

sections.label: MSF marriage cohort divorce report
sections.summary: An MSF report tracking 29 marriage cohorts from 1987 to 2015 found more divorces in earlier marriage years, highest between years five and 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a report from MSF, which tracked 29 cohorts of marriages between 1987 and 2015, more divorces are happening during the earlier years of a couple's marriage, with the highest proportion of couples ending their marriages between years five and 10.

sections.label: Subsidising marriage therapy suggestion
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to subsidise marriage therapy for couples in their fifth to 10th year of marriage, a critical vulnerable period with highest divorce cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we could go a step further and subsidise marriage therapy for couples who are between their fifth to 10th year of marriage, since it seems to be the critical period where marriages are vulnerable, and divorce cases are at their highest.

sections.label: Mandatory pre-divorce counselling consideration
sections.summary: MSF is asked to consider mandatory pre-divorce counselling for couples citing unreasonable behaviour and future DMA cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can MSF consider mandatory pre-divorce counselling for all couples who cite unreasonable behaviour as the reason for their divorce and, in future, the couples who cite DMA as a reason for the divorce?

sections.label: Sham divorce loophole concerns
sections.summary: The additions to section 95 raise concerns about sham divorces, identification, penalties, and calls for stronger marriage support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The proposed additions to section 95 of the Women's Charter will allow for couples to divorce by mutual agreement and I worry that this will become a loophole for sham divorces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: How would the Ministry identify such cases and are there penalties that will arise as a result of such fake divorces?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But it has also made divorce easier, inadvertently eroding the sanctity of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We should do more upstream to help strengthen marriages and prevent relationships from breaking down, through mandatory and extensive marriage preparation programmes and make marriage therapy, marriage counselling cheaper and more accessible.

sections.label: Renaming Women's Charter rejected
sections.summary: The Ministry will not rename the Women's Charter to the Family Charter as the marriage and divorce provisions are gender-neutral.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Louis Ng proposed renaming the Women's Charter to the Family Charter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We will not be doing so in today's amendments as, if we look at the provisions on marriage and divorce, the provisions are gender-neutral and do not discriminate in favour of men or women.

sections.label: Convictions for marriage offences
sections.summary: Between 2014 and 2021, 388 individuals were convicted for engaging in or arranging such marriages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Between 2014 and 2021, there have been 388 individuals convicted for engaging in or arranging such marriages.

sections.label: Marriage preparation programme rebates
sections.summary: Couples are encouraged to attend marriage preparation programmes, with rebates of $140 or $70 for supported programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we strongly encourage all couples to attend marriage preparation programmes and we provide rebates of $140 for couples to attend the 12-hour PREP workshop, or $70 for supported programmes offered by the community.

sections.label: MPP extension to minor children
sections.summary: All divorcing couples with minor children must attend MPP before filing, with priority on extending it regardless of fact cited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: With the amendments, all divorcing couples with minor children must attend MPP before filing for divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Mr Melvin Yong asked if this pre-divorce counselling could be extended to those who cite unreasonable behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We agree it is good to do so but our priority at this point is to extend MPP to all divorcing couples with minor children, regardless of the fact they cite.

sections.label: No mandated children's divorce programme
sections.summary: MSF considered mandating a programme for minor children of divorcing parents but decided parents must assume primary responsibility instead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MSF had considered mandating all minor children whose parents are undergoing divorce to attend a programme to help them cope better with the divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: However, we believe that parents, even as they undergo divorce, must still assume primary responsibility for their children's well-being rather than have the Government mandate a programme for their children.

sections.label: Enforcement orders and imprisonment
sections.summary: The Court will consider all aspects of a case, and imprisonment is intended only for egregious cases of non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Both Members also brought up the need for enforcement orders to be made judiciously, especially in the case of a term of imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I assure Members that the Court will take all aspects of the case into account in making its orders, including whether the child had refused access to the parent, and a term of imprisonment is intended to be imposed only on egregious cases of non-compliance.

sections.label: Safeguards before divorce finalised
sections.summary: Safeguards remain, including the three-year minimum marriage period, a three-month period before finalisation, and the existing five facts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For this reason, the safeguards to ensure the decision to divorce – that it is a considered one – remain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: These include: (a) the three-year minimum marriage period before a divorce can be filed; (b) a minimum three-month period before divorce is finalised; and (c) that the existing five facts for parties remain for parties who prefer to rely on them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In fact, citing DMA requires further submissions to the Court: (a) the reasons leading parties to conclude that their marriage has irretrievably broken down; (b) the efforts made by parties to reconcile; and (c) considerations given to the arrangements to be made in relation to the parties' children and financial affairs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It is also for this reason that we will not be reducing the three-year minimum marriage period before a divorce can be filed, as Ms Carrie Tan has suggested.

sections.label: Divorce before three-year minimum
sections.summary: Parties may seek the Court's permission to file for divorce before the three-year minimum marriage period in cases of exceptional hardship or depravity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In cases of exceptional hardship or depravity, parties may seek the Court's permission to file for divorce before the three-year minimum marriage period is up.

sections.label: DMA as sixth fact
sections.summary: DMA is a sixth fact to prove the sole ground of divorce through an agreement citing reasons, reconciliation efforts, and considerations for children and finances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Unlike other overseas regimes where parties are not required to prove that the marriage has irretrievably broken down, or where the filing for divorce by one party is sufficient to prove the marriage has irretrievably broken down, DMA is a sixth fact to prove the sole ground of divorce and it is done through an agreement that cites: one, reasons for the breakdown; two, efforts at reconciliation; and three, considerations for children and financial matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Under the Women’s Charter, the defendant is able to file a defence against a divorce application, irrespective of the fact cited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I would also like to assure Ms Sylvia Lim that we do not expect the number of divorces to increase significantly with the introduction of DMA.

sections.label: Acceptable reasons for DMA
sections.summary: Acceptable reasons for irretrievable breakdown could include deep-seated differences in values, avoiding blame on one party, and children should not be cited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Regarding the details of DMA, Ms Hany Soh asked what reasons are acceptable to substantiate that the marriage has irretrievably broken down.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This could include reasons, such as a deep-seated difference in values, and the intention is to avoid reasons that point blame only at one party, and children should not be cited as the reason for divorce.

sections.label: DMA as divorce fact
sections.summary: DMA is a different fact on which a divorce can be obtained, but it is not an easier fact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: DMA is a different fact on which you can obtain a divorce, but it is not an easier fact.

sections.label: Three-year divorce time bar
sections.summary: Parties must meet the three-year time bar before they can apply for divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In all cases, parties have to meet the three-year time bar before they can apply for divorce.

sections.label: Simplified Track divorce timelines
sections.summary: On the Simplified Track, filing to interim judgment takes about six to 12 weeks, then at least three months to final judgment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For couples who divorce on the Simplified Track, the time taken from filing to the grant of the interim judgment is approximately six to 12 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Thereafter, there would be another minimum period of three months to the final judgment.

sections.label: DMA agreement court assessment
sections.summary: For a DMA agreement, the Court must assess that parties act voluntarily and know the terms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Indeed, for an agreement to be made under DMA, the Court must, among other things, assess that parties are acting voluntarily and have the requisite knowledge of the terms.

sections.label: Filing after MPP refusal
sections.summary: If one party refuses to attend MPP, the other can still file for divorce after completing MPP themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In a case where one party refuses to attend MPP, the other party will still be able to proceed with the filing of the divorce after they have themselves completed MPP.

sections.label: Bailiff assistance only when necessary
sections.summary: Courts order bailiff's assistance only where their presence is absolutely necessary, not in all cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Courts will only order the bailiff’s assistance in cases where their presence is absolutely necessary, and not in all cases.

sections.label: Enforcement of maintenance orders study
sections.summary: MSF is working with MinLaw and the Family Justice Courts to study more efficient enforcement of maintenance orders and minimise repeat enforcement, considering amendments under separate legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I have said so earlier, MSF is working with MinLaw and the Family Justice Courts to study how to provide more efficient and effective enforcement of maintenance orders and to minimise repeat enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are considering the feasibility of taking up these amendments under a separate legislation.

sections.label: Maintenance for financially vulnerable parties
sections.summary: The current provision provides maintenance for parties who tend to be more financially vulnerable post-divorce, namely women and incapacitated men.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The current provision, therefore, provides maintenance for the parties who tend to be more financially vulnerable post-divorce – women and incapacitated men.

sections.label: Mandatory MPP before divorce filing
sections.summary: Under the proposed amendments, all parents with minor children must attend MPP before filing for divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: With the proposed amendments, all parents with minor children must attend MPP before they file for divorce.

sections.label: HDB agreement before listing child
sections.summary: HDB requires divorced parents to try to agree before listing their child in a flat application, and can waive the requirement case-by-case for those unable to agree or with low income and no other housing options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: HDB is not in a position to determine which parent can exercise the right to do so, and thus requires divorced parents to try to come to an agreement, in the first instance, before listing their child in a flat application.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I agree with Mr Ang Wei Neng that we must support those who face difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For those who are unable to reach an agreement with their ex-spouse or have low income and have no other housing options, HDB can exercise flexibility to waive the requirement on a case-by-case basis, to ensure that both parties have options to provide housing for themselves and their children.

sections.label: Timeline and community marriage efforts
sections.summary: Marriage-related and some divorce-related amendments are expected to come into effect in the latter half of this year, others such as DMA in 2023, with community efforts and a separate Bill on family violence planned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If passed in Parliament, we expect all the marriage-related amendments and some of the divorce-related amendments to come into effect in the latter half of this year, while others, such as DMA, would come into effect in 2023, to allow time for the Courts, lawyers, social service agencies and other parties to be ready.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Beyond legislation, it is truly the efforts of the community that will make a difference to those impacted by a divorce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I also urge experienced couples to do their part to actively mentor and counsel younger couples in their social circles or religious organisations, bolstering the efforts of licensed solemnisers under the JOY initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I also encourage passionate individuals and ground-up groups to partner MSF's Alliance for Action to organise family activities, programmes to strengthen marriages and family relationships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I am also excited to be working with Families for Life, a ground-up movement to build strong and resilient families in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: However, we also recognise that more can be done to enhance protection against violence, and we will be proposing amendments in a separate Bill by the end of this year to implement the recommendations of the Taskforce on Family Violence.

sections.label: Counselling direction and DMA requirements
sections.summary: If the Court had directed parties to counselling, they had not satisfied DMA requirements, so continuing divorce applications would require citing a different fact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If the Court had directed the parties to go for counselling, it would have meant that, in their application for DMA, they had not satisfied the requirements under DMA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As such, if the parties would still want to continue with their divorce applications, then they will have to cite a different fact.

sections.label: Parents MPP age limit
sections.summary: Parents of children who would benefit from MPP can do so even if the children have exceeded age 21.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Indeed, for children who would benefit from having their parents go for MPP, and, if they have exceeded the age limit of 21, the parents can similarly do so.

sections.label: Court child best interest
sections.summary: The Court will have to consider what is in the best interest of the child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the last point that the Member raised, the Court will have to consider what is in the best interest of the child.
